description: A school principal must approve the operating and purchasing plan for a new campus garden, including the bed construction method, work date, funding, protective equipment, and required records, with input from the science teacher, facilities coordinator, business manager, and school nurse.

shared_context.S1: The school has approved the concept of building a twelve-bed teaching garden beside the science wing.
shared_context.S2: The current draft plan uses in-ground beds, schedules the volunteer workday for October 18, estimates a $3,000 charge to general funds, and lists standard latex gardening gloves.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Morgan has final authority to approve the garden's construction, purchasing, and safety plan.
shared_context.S4: The school's weekly project huddle is used to confirm site, purchasing, and student-safety requirements before a principal signs a campus project plan.
shared_context.S5: At the project huddle, Dr. Morgan asks the science teacher, facilities coordinator, business manager, and school nurse to report any requirements they have verified.

PF1.text: Ms. Rivera's soil test from the proposed garden area measured lead at 180 parts per million; the district garden standard requires removing the top six inches of soil and using raised beds at that reading. She received the laboratory result yesterday, after the draft plan was circulated, and has not yet entered it in the project folder.

PF2.text: Mr. Chen's utility-locate request cleared the site for work on October 28 but not before that date, and facilities policy requires a posted site permit before excavation or bed assembly. The locate response arrived this morning after the draft workday was proposed.

PF3.text: Ms. Brooks confirmed that a community-garden grant will reimburse up to exactly $4,200, but only purchases covered by a purchase order issued before ordering can use the grant. The grant office sent its award confirmation to her yesterday, and she has not yet attached it to the draft budget.

PF4.text: Nurse Williams' student health review identified a documented severe latex allergy among the students scheduled for garden instruction; the school safety protocol therefore requires nitrile-only gloves and an allergy-safety notice at the garden entrance. She completed the review this week, after the draft equipment list was prepared.

acceptance_conditions: The garden must use six inches of soil removal and raised beds.
The volunteer workday must be scheduled for October 28.
The project must use the community-garden grant with a $4,200 budget.
All garden gloves must be nitrile-only.
A facilities permit must be posted before work begins.
A grant purchase order must be issued before ordering.
An allergy-safety notice must be posted at the garden entrance.
The soil finding must be cited by the principal as justification.

content_checks.C1: 'raised beds' in decisions['bed_construction'] and 'six inches' in decisions['bed_construction']
content_checks.C3: 'community-garden grant' in decisions['funding_source'] and '$4,200' in decisions['funding_source']
content_checks.C5: any('site permit' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any('purchase order' in c['detail'] and 'before ordering' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('allergy-safety notice' in c['detail'] and 'garden entrance' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The 180-parts-per-million soil result changes construction from in-ground beds to removal of exactly six inches of soil followed by raised beds, and supplies the required cited justification.
The utility-locate clearance changes the workday from October 18 to exactly October 28 and makes a posted facilities permit mandatory before work.
The confirmed grant changes funding to the community-garden grant with an exact $4,200 budget and requires a purchase order before any ordering.
The documented severe latex allergy changes the equipment choice to nitrile-only gloves and requires an allergy-safety notice at the garden entrance.
